purpose: Keep the Field Tools clear on first reading and recognizably in Nic Payne’s voice.

references.lesson: Begin with a specific human situation; earn the larger argument through it.
Use conversational rhythm, warmth, self-awareness, and occasional humor. Explain ideas through everyday experience.
Use dialogue and concrete images to make the point; examine the conditions without turning colleagues into villains.

rules: Name who is doing what, for whom, and why it matters. Do not make readers supply the missing scene.
Write something a person could comfortably say aloud. Use contractions and connected sentences; do not turn every thought into a slogan.
Keep form labels literal and ask one clear question. Use hints for necessary context and examples.
Keep the depth and care for people. Plain language must not reduce the work to filling boxes or winning arguments.
Use humor sparingly in guidance; never at the expense of the person the reader needs to work with.
Do not invent personal stories or experiences for Nic. Mark invented product examples as fictional.
Keep a proposal distinct from an agreement, a prediction distinct from an observed result, and private reflection out of shared outputs.
AI Stalemate PM and Lead Developer paths must address each audience directly, including its own concerns and private reflection.
When copy changes, update public pages, Guides, Labs, examples, generated documents, PDFs, and product previews together.

examples.after: fix the broken invitation link that stops new customers joining their account
correct the figures in a customer’s monthly report

examples.before: establish what would move and who can approve the tradeoff
examples.after: ask the team what would have to wait, then take that choice to the person who can decide
